financial_flags.finding: Revenue has declined two years in a row: $2,700.5M (FY24), $2,490.8M (FY25), $2,446.0M (FY26).
financial_flags.why: Profitability was reached on shrinking sales, so it relies on cost cuts rather than growth.

financial_flags.finding: Total liabilities ($2,195.6M) exceed total assets ($2,055.9M) at FY26, a deficit of about $139.7M (my calculation). The gap has narrowed from FY25.
financial_flags.why: Negative book equity limits the balance-sheet cushion.

financial_flags.finding: Long-term debt is $1,330.0M against cash of $1,206.6M. Interest expense is cited at $123.8M and $134.5M in two periods.
financial_flags.why: Net debt is modest, but interest costs are heavy relative to FY26 net income of $63.2M.

financial_flags.finding: The turn to profit is recent: net income was $63.2M in FY26 after losses of $118.9M (FY25) and $551.9M (FY24).
financial_flags.why: One profitable year is a short record. Sustainability is not yet proven.

risks.finding: The Term Loan and revolver carry covenants. When the revolver is drawn, liquidity must be at least $250M and trailing subscription revenue at least $1.2B. Total indebtedness is about $1.3B, including $350M of 5.50% convertible notes due 2029.
risks.evidence_quote: requires us, when revolving loans are outstanding, to maintain a total level of liquidity of not less than $250.0 million

risks.finding: The company faces ongoing class actions, personal injury claims and government inquiries tied to the Tread+ and Bike recalls. A further recall of Original Series Bike+ units was announced in November 2025.
risks.evidence_quote: We have been and in some cases continue to be subject to class action litigation, private personal injury claims

risks.finding: Profitability may not be sustained. The company has a history of operating losses, and subscriber retention and demand are uncertain.
risks.evidence_quote: Although we reported net income in fiscal year 2026, we have incurred significant operating losses in prior periods

risks.finding: Material weaknesses were identified in internal controls in FY2021 to FY2024. Controls are now reported effective, but the risk of recurrence is flagged, including in physical inventory verification at last-mile partners.
risks.evidence_quote: we identified certain material weaknesses in our internal control over financial reporting.

risks.finding: Demand forecasting and inventory risk. Past demand declines led to write-downs, discounting and disputes with suppliers over purchase commitments.
risks.evidence_quote: We have in recent periods experienced, and may continue to experience decreases in consumer demand, resulting in inventory write-downs

risks.finding: The company relies on contract manufacturers, often a single supplier. Their facilities are concentrated in Taiwan, China and Thailand, which adds supply-chain and tariff exposure.
risks.evidence_quote: In most cases, we rely on only a single supplier for our products and some critical components.

red_flags.evidence_quote: We have been and in some cases continue to be subject to class action litigation, private personal injury claims and other regulatory proceedings

rating_rationale: Peloton reached net income of $63.2M in FY26 and cash rose to $1,206.6M. Liabilities fell, and management reports effective internal controls (9A-p005) with an Ernst & Young attestation. No going-concern language was found. Offsetting this, revenue has fallen two years running, and liabilities still exceed assets. About $1.3B of debt carries covenants and high interest costs. Recall-related class actions and injury claims continue. Material weaknesses existed through FY2024, though the 10-K describes them as previously identified. Rating: medium. The material_weakness flag is marked not_found because the weaknesses were remediated and FY26 controls are effective. Research only, not investment advice.
open_questions: Review Note 12 (Commitments and Contingencies) for the size of the recall litigation exposure and any accruals.
Check the subscription revenue trend against the $1.2B trailing covenant minimum and the headroom on it.
Look at what drove the FY26 profit, including cost cuts, restructuring and one-time items, and whether margins are sustainable.
Check the maturity and refinancing plan for the Term Loan and notes (2029) and the dilution from the convertible notes.
Confirm that the material weaknesses are fully remediated and that the shared-services transition has not weakened controls.
Confirm there was no auditor change in recent years (none was found in the 10-K text searched).
